statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 15 of 100 in the low band, ten points below the 25 block threshold, while stress eases to 79 at the top of the high band and confidence stays high at 88.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The decisive evidence remains the price path: the 29,499.50 pre-bell high has now capped NQ for roughly four hours while price rotates about 56 points beneath it, and the cash index trades 29,451.66 against an unbroken 29,473.12 high. A market that keeps returning inside its range under a fixed ceiling is still granting mean reversion. The named window covers 19:00 to 21:00 UTC, the final cash hour into the 20:00 UTC close on a Friday weekly expiry and the thin post-close hour before the 21:00 UTC weekend halt, where conditional tail peaks at 18 and remains inside the low band. From 21:00 UTC the horizon is entirely inside the CME weekend closure, so conditional tail falls to a 5 to 7 floor. Stress stays high because the Hormuz conflict, crude near 100 dollars and an FOMC week that now prices a hike heavily are unresolved, but stress alone does not move the mapped state.
headline: The ceiling still holds and the volatility bid keeps draining: NQ trades 29,443.00 (+1.06%) about 56 points under a 29,499.50 high unbroken for four hours, NDX is 29,451.66 for a 1.20% gain beneath an intact 29,473.12 high, VIX is 15.71 at a session low and down 11.9%, and WTI has retreated to 99.52 on Oman-track Hormuz diplomacy. Tail is 15 in the low band; stress eases to 79.
body:
Both dated U.S. releases for Friday are verified and behind the market. The Bureau of Labor Statistics published the August consumer price report at 12:30 UTC: all items rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% over twelve months, while all items less food and energy rose 0.3% on the month, a tenth above consensus, and 2.4% over the year. The University of Michigan preliminary September survey followed at 14:00 UTC at 47.8 against a 51.0 consensus and a 51.7 August final, with year-ahead inflation expectations rising to 4.6% from 4.0%.

The price path remains the decisive evidence and its character has not changed. NQ trades 29,443.00 inside a 29,040.50 to 29,499.50 range, essentially unchanged against the 29,444.75 observed an hour earlier. The 29,499.50 high was set before the cash bell and has now capped the market for roughly four hours. The cash index has firmed back toward its own high, printing 29,451.66 for a 1.20% gain against an intact 29,473.12 session high, but that high has not been taken out either. A market that has spent four hours rotating inside a 459-point range beneath a fixed ceiling is not producing the persistent no-retracement extension that the tail score measures, which is why tail holds at 15 rather than building toward the block threshold.

Volatility continues to drain rather than expand. VIX is 15.71, down 11.9% on the day and sitting at its 15.67 session low after an intraday high of 17.71. A third consecutive hour of volatility decay through a post-release afternoon is characteristic of orderly price discovery.

Cross-asset evidence is split rather than aligned, which is the clearest argument against a higher tail. Equities are broadly higher while crude has fallen sharply, with WTI at 99.52, down 2.9%, and Brent at 104.24, down 3.2%, after reports of Iranian plans for talks with Gulf states in Oman. The curve is pulling in two directions: the 2-year yield is firmer at about 4.63% on the hawkish core print while the 10-year has eased to roughly 4.95% on the oil retreat. Delayed latest-session context from the shared collector shows index futures higher by about 1%, VIX futures down 8.4%, all eight tracked megacaps positive and six of seven tracked semiconductors positive; that breadth is genuinely aligned, but under the standing evidence rules aligned breadth amplifies tail only when live structure also shows mean-reversion failure, and live structure shows the opposite.

Stress eases one point to 79 and crosses into the high band. The two dated events of the day have both been absorbed without disorder, volatility has decayed for three hours and oil has given back part of its conflict premium. What keeps stress near the top of that band is unresolved rather than current: the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted with transit far below baseline, crude sits near 100 dollars with U.S. diesel at a record, consumer sentiment has collapsed to 47.8 with inflation expectations rising, and market pricing for next week's FOMC decision has moved sharply toward a rate increase over the course of this week.

The forward window is unusual in shape. Only the next four hours contain a tradable price path. The 19:00 UTC hour carries the conditional peak at 18 because a Friday weekly expiry, the 20:00 UTC closing auction and positioning into an FOMC week all land together. From the 21:00 UTC weekend halt the remaining twenty slots contain no price path at all, so conditional tail falls to a 5 to 7 floor while stress decays more slowly toward the moderate band, reflecting risk that accumulates for the Sunday reopen rather than risk that can be expressed inside the horizon.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 17:00 UTC on 10 September to 16:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 15 with the mode mixed and rises to 19 and 18 in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots around the previous cash close, the only event/whipsaw readings of the first half. The overnight hours from 22:00 UTC normalised into an 11 to 15 band, the quietest stretch of the window, with stress pinned in the mid-80s throughout. From 06:00 UTC the mode turned trend-up at tail 13, 14, 13, 14, 15 and 14 as the pre-report advance extended while stress eased from 85 to 82. The two highest readings of the whole window are the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC CPI hours at tail 21 and 22, the only slots mapped to WATCH and yellow, with confidence dropping to 70 and 80 as the release was absorbed. From 14:00 UTC the mode returned to mixed and tail settled back to 15, 16 and 15 with stress declining 82, 81, 80 and confidence restored to 87 and 88, which is the state this assessment continues.
outlookSummary: The forward window covers only four hours of tradable session and then spends its remaining twenty slots inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail opens at 15 in the current slot, which contains observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds 15 for the 18:00 UTC budget statement and peaks at 18 in the 19:00 UTC final cash hour, where Friday weekly-expiry unwind and closing-auction flow concentrate ahead of an FOMC week. It settles to 15 for the thin post-close hour into the halt. Those two hours form the named 19:00 to 21:00 UTC window, and every slot in the horizon stays inside the low band and maps to EA_ON. From 21:00 UTC conditional tail collapses to a 5 to 7 floor because no price path exists for mean reversion to fail against, while stress decays more slowly from 57 to 33 across the weekend, tracking the thinning information environment rather than any resolution of the Hormuz conflict or next week's Fed decision. Confidence declines from 88 to 66 across the horizon purely as a function of distance from the assessment. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen and the FOMC week that follows fall outside this horizon.
